notes: Summary: SaaS vendor building a hosted knowledge-base RAG product for customers. Primary flows: 1) high-QPS customer-facing search (autocomplete + top-k) 2) server-side cross-encoder rerank for final result set. Indexing scale: ~150k-300k docs (moderate), avg doc size 800-1,200 tokens. Traffic profile: sustained 400-600 QPS, peak 1k QPS during morning batch windows. Latency targets: end-to-end retrieval + rerank p95 < 200ms (ideal p95 < 120ms for premium customers). Cost sensitivity: target gross cost per query <$0.005 at typical traffic; procurement will balk if >$0.01/query.
architecture_notes: They plan hybrid pipeline: vector search (ann) to pull top-100 then cross-encoder rerank on top-10. Prefer hosted API for ease of ops; want routing policies if multi-region and automatic fallback. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization profiles to reduce cost on reranker. Asking about prefix/KV caching for repeated queries (customer chat sessions).
security_and_compliance: Requirements: SSO (SAML) for admin console, audit logging for queries (90d retention), US data residency, KMS integration for key management. SOC2 in progress; will require KBA on audit log export and access controls.
poC_criteria: 1) Demonstrate sustained 500 QPS retrieval+rerank with p95 <200ms for sample corpus (150k docs). 2) Cost estimate from Redwood Optimize showing cost/Q <= $0.005 at target QPS. 3) SAML SSO and encrypted audit logging proof-of-concept. 4) Simple canary rollback for model variant fallback.
commercial_notes: Estimated ARR target for first year $75k-$250k. Prefers annual commit if latency/cost guarantees met. Ask: dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs; will only consider Dedicated if hosted can't meet latency/cost with predictable pricing.
quotes: We need reranker latency to feel instant to end users — sub-200ms is the difference between 'good' and 'too slow'
